frequency_question: How often do formal agency recognition withdrawal or revocation proceedings against a major institutional accreditor result in a final revocation order within a two-year window of observation?
membership_rule: Includes any instance where a federal oversight agency initiates formal proceedings to strip an institutional or professional accreditor of its official recognition status, where a final determination is reached within a multi-year window. Excludes voluntary relinquishments or routine periodic renewals without contested termination proceedings.

cases.name: American Bar Association recognition review (prior challenge cycles)
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) first termination
ACICS second termination (after reinstatement and subsequent review)
American Bar Association compliance review regarding standards and bar passage

coverage_note: 4 prominent historical oversight and revocation challenge cycles identified in modern administrative history; 2 resulted in terminal revocation.
known_gaps: Excludes minor compliance warnings and informal secretarial advisories that did not advance to formal de-recognition or termination dockets.
skeleton: Sector-wide major institutional and professional accreditor oversight reviews resulting in contested revocation proceedings over the past three decades.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 4 major contested review cycles = 50% base historical rate for contested proceedings culminating in revocation when advanced signals of high tension are present.
validity_reason: Administrative procedures governing the National Advisory Committee on Institutional Quality and Integrity (NACIQI) and Department of Education recognition standards remain stable across typical multi-year regulatory cycles.
